title: 349: The Birth of the United States (Part 3)

sentences.en: The sun never shone on a cause of greater worth.
sentences.zh: 从未有过比这更值得奋斗的事业。

sentences.en: It is not the affair of a city, a county, a province, or a kingdom, but of a continent, of at least one-eighth part of the habitable globe.
sentences.zh: 这不仅是一座城市、一个县、一个省或一个王国的事，而是一个大陆的事，至少是这颗宜居星球八分之一领土的事。

sentences.en: It is not the concern of a day, a year, or an age.
sentences.zh: 这也不仅仅是一天、一年或一个时代所关心的事。

sentences.en: Posterity are virtually involved in the contest, and will be more or less affected, even to the end of time, by the proceedings now.
sentences.zh: 后代子孙实际上也卷入了这场斗争，并将或多或少地受到当下所作所为的影响，直至时间的尽头。

sentences.en: Oh, ye that love mankind!
sentences.zh: 噢，你们这些热爱人类的人！

sentences.en: Ye that dare oppose not only the tyranny, but the tyrant!
sentences.zh: 你们这些敢于不仅反抗暴政，更敢于反抗暴君的人！

sentences.en: Stand forth!
sentences.zh: 站出来吧！

sentences.en: Every spot of the old world is overrun with oppression.
sentences.zh: 旧世界的每一寸土地都充斥着压迫。

sentences.en: Freedom hath been hunted round the globe.
sentences.zh: 自由已在全球范围内遭到追捕。

sentences.en: Asia and Africa have long expelled her.
sentences.zh: 亚洲和非洲早已将她驱逐。

sentences.en: Europe regards her like a stranger.
sentences.zh: 欧洲视她如陌路。

sentences.en: And England hath given her warning to depart.
sentences.zh: 而英格兰也已向她下达了逐客令。

sentences.en: Oh, receive the fugitive, and prepare in time an asylum for all mankind.
sentences.zh: 噢，接纳这位逃亡者吧，及时为全人类准备一个避难所。

sentences.en: So that, Dominic, was son of East Anglia.
sentences.zh: 所以，多米尼克，他是东盎格利亚之子。

sentences.en: Tom Paine, radical, enthusiast for revolution, and specifically in this context, author of pamphlet Common Sense, which came out in January 1776.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·潘恩，激进派，革命狂热者，特别是在此背景下，他是小册子《常识》的作者，该书于1776年1月出版。

sentences.en: And we've got Adam Smith with us.
sentences.zh: 我们还有亚当·斯密在场。

sentences.en: Adam, am I right in saying that this is really the first kind of mass market pamphlet that argues for removing America's links with the British monarchy?
sentences.zh: 亚当，我说这是第一本真正意义上主张切断美国与英国君主制联系的大众市场小册子，对吗？

sentences.en: It was genuinely a bestseller, genuinely a bestseller.
sentences.zh: 它确实是一本畅销书，名副其实的畅销书。

sentences.en: And it was subsidised, and it was circulated across all of the 13 colonies.
sentences.zh: 它得到了资助，并在所有13个殖民地广泛流传。

sentences.en: And it was, as you say, the first pamphlet to explicitly and clearly make the case not only for independence, but a positive case for republicanism.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，它是第一本不仅明确且清晰地提出独立主张，还为共和主义提供了积极论证的小册子。

sentences.en: So, hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 那么，大家好。

sentences.en: Just to give you a bit of context, if you're just tuning in, this is the third in our series on the American Revolution.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家了解背景，如果你刚加入我们，这是我们关于美国革命系列节目的第三期。

sentences.en: We have had the Boston Tea Party.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讲过了波士顿倾茶事件。

sentences.en: We've had the Battle of Bunker Hill.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讲过了邦克山战役。

sentences.en: The colonies have been declared by George III as being an open revolt.
sentences.zh: 乔治三世已经宣布殖民地处于公开叛乱状态。

sentences.en: And we are now in January 1776 for the publication of this extraordinary pamphlet.
sentences.zh: 现在我们来到了1776年1月，这本非凡小册子的出版之时。

sentences.en: Half a million copies of Adam, I think, get sold by the end of the year.
sentences.zh: 亚当，我想到年底卖出了五十万册。

sentences.en: And Thomas Paine, the irony is he's not actually American.
sentences.zh: 而托马斯·潘恩，讽刺的是，他其实不是美国人。

sentences.en: So, he's gone to America, but he is, as Tom's exquisite impression suggests, he's from Thetford in Norfolk.
sentences.zh: 所以，他去了美国，但正如汤姆那精彩的模仿所暗示的，他来自诺福克的塞特福德。

sentences.en: And he used to make corsets, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想他以前是做紧身胸衣的。

sentences.en: I think that was in Sussex.
sentences.zh: 我想那是在萨塞克斯郡。

sentences.en: He moved to Lewis.
sentences.zh: 他搬到了刘易斯。

sentences.en: To make the corsets in Lewis.
sentences.zh: 去刘易斯做紧身胸衣。

sentences.en: I believe so, yes.
sentences.zh: 我想是的，没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, and he'd twice been sacked as a customs officer, ironically,
sentences.zh: 嗯，讽刺的是，他曾两次被解雇，作为一名海关官员，

sentences.en: for incompetence and corruption, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为无能和腐败。

sentences.en: So, are you a big Thomas Paine fan, Adam?
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，你是托马斯·潘恩的忠实粉丝吗？

sentences.en: I'm not, really, I have to say, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 说实话，多米尼克，我并不是。

sentences.en: I do admire the muscularity of his prose.
sentences.zh: 我确实钦佩他文字的力量感。

sentences.en: And common sense is you can see why it was so effective.
sentences.zh: 而且你可以看出《常识》为什么会如此有效。

sentences.en: It doesn't have all the Latin tags and all the learned references that most of the pamphlets of the American Revolution did.
sentences.zh: 它没有美国革命时期大多数小册子中那种拉丁语标签和博学的引经据典。

sentences.en: Whenever I think of Thomas Paine, though, I think about what happened to his body after he died.
sentences.zh: 不过，每当我想起托马斯·潘恩，我就会想到他死后发生的事情。

sentences.en: Do you know this story?
sentences.zh: 你知道这个故事吗？

sentences.en: He died in obscurity.
sentences.zh: 他在默默无闻中去世。

sentences.en: And, of course, he was very unpopular by the end of his life, including in America.
sentences.zh: 当然，在他生命尽头，他非常不受欢迎，包括在美国。

sentences.en: But his great British admirer, the radical William Cobbett, went to America and brought back his body to England,
sentences.zh: 但他伟大的英国崇拜者，激进派威廉·科贝特去了美国，把他的遗体带回了英国，

sentences.en: hoping that his admirers in England would create some kind of great tomb around it.
sentences.zh: 希望他在英国的崇拜者能为他建造一座宏伟的陵墓。

sentences.en: He couldn't raise the money to do so.
sentences.zh: 但他没能筹集到足够的资金。

sentences.en: So, kind of very Lenin behaviour.
sentences.zh: 所以，这行为有点像列宁。

sentences.en: So, he kept the bones of Thomas Paine in a box in his house.
sentences.zh: 他把托马斯·潘恩的骨头装在一个盒子里，放在家里。

sentences.en: And when he died, they were sold with his effects.
sentences.zh: 他死后，这些骨头连同他的遗物一起被卖掉了。

sentences.en: And nobody knows what happened to them.
sentences.zh: 没人知道它们去了哪里。

sentences.en: And there's some of them, some bones have turned up in Australia quite recently.
sentences.zh: 最近在澳大利亚出现了一些骨头。

sentences.en: And there's bits of Thomas Paine all over the world.
sentences.zh: 托马斯·潘恩的遗骨散落在世界各地。

sentences.en: So, poor old Thomas Paine ended badly, even beyond his life.
sentences.zh: 所以，可怜的托马斯·潘恩结局很惨，甚至在他死后也是如此。

sentences.en: But you probably didn't want me to quite go there.
sentences.zh: 但你可能不想让我讲这些。

sentences.en: No, that's great.
sentences.zh: 不，这很棒。

sentences.en: To go back to common sense.
sentences.zh: 回到《常识》上来。

sentences.en: I mean, this has a massive impact, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这产生了巨大的影响，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes, it really does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And he is the author of these resonant phrases.
sentences.zh: 他是这些响亮短语的作者。

sentences.en: And you read some of them out just then, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你刚才读了一些。

sentences.en: The cause of America is the cause of all mankind.
sentences.zh: 美国的事业就是全人类的事业。

sentences.en: I mean, that's not only is that a great phrase, that is, in many ways, it seems to me, the key to understanding American political culture.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不仅是一个伟大的短语，在我看来，它在很多方面都是理解美国政治文化的关键。

sentences.en: That what happens in America, the cause of this revolution, everything we do in America,
sentences.zh: 在美国发生的事情，这场革命的事业，我们在美国所做的一切，

sentences.en: our purpose is transcendental meaning.
sentences.zh: 我们的目的具有超验的意义。

sentences.en: We are providentially blessed in some important way.
sentences.zh: 我们在某种重要方面受到了天意的眷顾。

sentences.en: The cause of America is the cause of mankind.
sentences.zh: 美国的事业就是人类的事业。

sentences.en: What happens here has universal significance.
sentences.zh: 发生在这里的事情具有普遍的意义。

sentences.en: But when it comes out, is there a sense in which, as well as enthusing the revolution, inspiring kind of an upsurge of backing for republicanism,
sentences.zh: 但当它出版时，除了激发革命、鼓舞对共和主义的支持浪潮之外，

sentences.en: are there also conservatives among the revolutionaries who become a bit nervous about this, who kind of pull back from...
sentences.zh: 革命者中是否也有保守派对此感到不安，从而开始退缩……

sentences.en: John Adams, for example, doesn't like common sense at all.
sentences.zh: 例如，约翰·亚当斯就一点也不喜欢《常识》。

sentences.en: He thinks he's badly argued based on abstractions.
sentences.zh: 他认为这基于抽象概念，论证得很糟糕。

sentences.en: You know, John Adams is a serious man who thinks that the business of governments and constitution writing, which he loves, I mean, he likes the business of constitution writing,
sentences.zh: 你知道，约翰·亚当斯是一个严肃的人，他认为政府事务和宪法起草——他很喜欢，我是说，他喜欢起草宪法的工作，

sentences.en: but he thinks it's a serious business of balancing interests.
sentences.zh: 但他认为这是平衡利益的严肃工作。

sentences.en: It's not about all this kind of blue skies thinking, these grand abstractions.
sentences.zh: 这与那种空想、宏大的抽象概念无关。

sentences.en: And he thinks it's very dangerous, the direction that Thomas Paine is going, including the practical suggestions that Paine is making about how a republic,
sentences.zh: 他认为托马斯·潘恩所走的方向非常危险，包括潘恩对共和国应该是什么样子的实际建议，

sentences.en: once you've overthrown the king and the British Empire, should look.
sentences.zh: 一旦你推翻了国王和大英帝国。

sentences.en: And John Adams doesn't want the debtors and the poor farmers in the western parts of the estates to be running these new independent estates, should it come to that.
sentences.zh: 约翰·亚当斯可不希望债务人和西部各州的贫苦农民来管理这些新的独立州，如果真走到那一步的话。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of nervousness as well as enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 所以除了热情，还有很多不安。

sentences.en: And before we get into Adams and what happens next, to go back to that thing of the cause of America is the cause of all mankind.
sentences.zh: 在我们深入探讨亚当斯和接下来发生的事情之前，回到“美国的事业就是全人类的事业”这一点上。

sentences.en: At this point, does the rest of mankind care?
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，全人类的其他部分关心吗？

sentences.en: I mean, are people watching?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有人在看吗？

sentences.en: I mean, there's always that sort of sense in America, isn't there, that the world is watching.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，美国总有一种感觉，不是吗，全世界都在看着。

sentences.en: I mean, it's been chanted so many times by protesters, demonstrators through American history.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在美国历史上，抗议者和示威者已经无数次高呼这一点。

sentences.en: The eyes of the world are on us, the shot heard around the world.
sentences.zh: 全世界的目光都在注视着我们，那声震惊世界的枪响。

sentences.en: But is the world watching at the beginning of 1776?
sentences.zh: 但在1776年初，世界在注视吗？

sentences.en: It's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: And I think often the answer is that a lot of the world, anyway, is watching.
sentences.zh: 我认为答案往往是，无论如何，世界很大一部分确实在注视。

sentences.en: And that's why they're often right to say that, the eyes of the world are upon us, which is the John Winthrop phrase from the 17th century,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们说“全世界的目光都在注视着我们”往往是对的，这是17世纪约翰·温斯罗普的短语，

sentences.en: which was being revived at around about this time or a little bit later, that what happens here matters.
sentences.zh: 在当时或稍晚一点被重新提起，即发生在这里的事情很重要。

sentences.en: And there were always, at this time and later and earlier, plenty of people outside of America, people who'd never been there, people who dreamed of America,
sentences.zh: 在当时、后来以及更早的时候，美国之外总有很多人，从未去过那里的人，梦想着美国的人，

sentences.en: who projected onto America a kind of vision of the good society, who wanted America to be the future.
sentences.zh: 他们将一种美好社会的愿景投射到美国身上，他们希望美国成为未来。

sentences.en: And what Paine was saying in common sense were the sorts of things that radicals in Britain had been saying for years.
sentences.zh: 潘恩在《常识》中所说的话，正是英国激进派多年来一直在说的话。

sentences.en: And the attacks on the king, which were quite crude and extreme, but which were the sorts of things that you would hear in radical circles in Britain in the 17th century.
sentences.zh: 而对国王的攻击，虽然相当粗鲁和极端，但也是你在17世纪英国激进圈子里会听到的那种话。

sentences.en: So the royal brute calling him that kind of, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以称他为“皇家畜生”，那种，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And to go back now to the sort of military strategic picture, the British had, they'd been in Boston, but they basically realised they can't,
sentences.zh: 现在回到军事战略层面，英国人，他们曾驻扎在波士顿，但他们基本上意识到他们不能，

sentences.en: they're trapped in Boston, they have to get out.
sentences.zh: 他们被困在波士顿，必须撤离。

sentences.en: So a couple of months after Paine publishes that pamphlet,
sentences.zh: 所以潘恩出版那本小册子几个月后，

sentences.en: General Howe, William Howe, who is the commander in Boston, says, okay, out.
sentences.zh: 波士顿的指挥官威廉·豪将军说，好吧，撤。

sentences.en: And they evacuate the city completely.
sentences.zh: 他们完全撤离了这座城市。

sentences.en: I mean, the city that's been the cockpit of revolution, they take some of the loyal, several thousand loyalists with them who they'd dump in Halifax in Canada.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这座曾经是革命核心的城市，他们带走了一些效忠派，几千名效忠派，把他们扔在加拿大的哈利法克斯。

sentences.en: And then they come down and establish themselves in New York.
sentences.zh: 然后他们南下，在纽约建立了据点。

sentences.en: New York, which we haven't mentioned really at all, actually, in the preceding two episodes.
sentences.zh: 纽约，我们在前两集里其实根本没提到过。

sentences.en: But New York, which has a,
sentences.zh: 但纽约，它有一个，

sentences.en: I mean, I don't know anything about this period at all, but is New York a more loyal city than Boston?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我对这段时期一无所知，但纽约比波士顿更忠诚吗？

sentences.en: Yes, yes, it definitely is.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: And there are certainly, there's a stronghold of loyalism in New York.
sentences.zh: 纽约确实有一个效忠派的堡垒。

sentences.en: It's not a straight, but there had been some conflicts with the New York legislature earlier on over the Quartering Act and things.
sentences.zh: 这并不简单，但早些时候纽约立法机构确实因《驻军法》等问题发生过冲突。

sentences.en: So it's not quite as straightforward as that.
sentences.zh: 所以情况并没有那么简单。

sentences.en: But certainly the British had reason to believe that if they wanted to create a beachhead, then New York was a good place to do it.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，英国人有理由相信，如果他们想建立一个滩头阵地，那么纽约是一个好地方。

sentences.en: Also, because it, of course, is at one end of the Hudson River Valley.
sentences.zh: 而且，因为它当然位于哈德逊河谷的一端。

sentences.en: So the idea was, if you can send a force down from Canada, from Quebec City, and up from New York and control the Hudson Valley, then you cut off New England.
sentences.zh: 所以当时的想法是，如果你能从加拿大、从魁北克城派出一支部队，再从纽约北上，控制哈德逊河谷，那么你就切断了新英格兰。

sentences.en: And then there's still this notion that New England is the problem.
sentences.zh: 而且当时仍然存在一种观念，即新英格兰是问题的根源。

sentences.en: So if you cut them off from the rest of the colonies, that would be a good strategic move to make.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你把他们从其他殖民地中切断，那将是一个很好的战略举措。

sentences.en: So that's another reason why New York is the focus at that point in 1776.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么纽约在1776年那个时候成为焦点的另一个原因。

sentences.en: But while the British are sort of working out what their strategic plan is going to be, their authority is pretty much collapsed across the colonies.
sentences.zh: 但当英国人还在制定他们的战略计划时，他们的权威在各殖民地几乎已经崩溃。

sentences.en: People aren't listening to their officials.
sentences.zh: 人们不再听从他们的官员。

sentences.en: People have set up their own town committees of safety or whatever.
sentences.zh: 人们建立了他们自己的城镇安全委员会之类的组织。

sentences.en: And the Second Continental Congress is still going.
sentences.zh: 第二届大陆会议仍在进行。

sentences.en: That's right, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 没错，是吧？

sentences.en: And they are where?
sentences.zh: 他们在哪里？

sentences.en: They are in Philadelphia now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在在费城。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they are busy with the business of government.
sentences.zh: 他们正忙于政府事务。

sentences.en: They have no formal authority to do so, but they are communicating with the colonies who are often now already being referred to as states
sentences.zh: 他们没有正式的权力这样做，但他们正在与各殖民地沟通，这些殖民地现在通常被称为“州”，

sentences.en: and saying, you've got to get your house in order, set up a government.
sentences.zh: 并说，你们得整顿好内部，建立一个政府。

sentences.en: Clearly, the external authority has collapsed.
sentences.zh: 显然，外部权威已经崩溃。

sentences.en: They, in the end, of course, do turn their attention to formal things like, well, are we declaring independence or not?
sentences.zh: 最终，他们当然会将注意力转向正式事务，比如，好吧，我们是否要宣布独立？

sentences.en: But most of the business of the Second Continental Congress up until this point is just preparing for war and trying to keep the business of government going.
sentences.zh: 但第二届大陆会议到目前为止的大部分工作只是为战争做准备，并试图维持政府的运作。

sentences.en: But that's the key thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但那是关键所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: Which I hadn't properly appreciated is that with the collapse of British rule and without the announcement of a kind of new state to replace it, everything is in limbo.
sentences.zh: 我之前没有充分意识到的是，随着英国统治的崩溃，在没有宣布建立某种新国家来取代它的情况下，一切都处于悬而未决的状态。

sentences.en: Tax collection, the entire functioning of government.
sentences.zh: 税收征管，整个政府的运作。

sentences.en: And John Adams, who I keep on invoking, I don't quite like John Adams really, and he's fundamental in some ways quite a conservative figure.
sentences.zh: 而约翰·亚当斯，我一直在引用他，我其实不太喜欢约翰·亚当斯，他在某些方面本质上是一个相当保守的人物。

sentences.en: And his view at the beginning of 1776 is basically, thank goodness that our independence has in practice been declared by the British government,
sentences.zh: 他在1776年初的观点基本上是，谢天谢地，我们的独立实际上已经被英国政府宣布了，

sentences.en: referring to the Prohibitory Act at the end of 1775, which prohibited all trade, the whole of the 13 colonies, that isolated all the 13, extending the coercive acts
sentences.zh: 指的是1775年底的《禁止贸易法》，该法案禁止了所有贸易，针对全部13个殖民地，孤立了所有13个殖民地，将强制法案

sentences.en: from Massachusetts to the whole of the colonies.
sentences.zh: 从马萨诸塞扩展到了所有殖民地。

sentences.en: I mean, for Adams, that was effectively the British government saying, you are now on your own and we are at war with you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对亚当斯来说，这实际上是英国政府在说，你们现在自求多福吧，我们正在与你们交战。

sentences.en: It was them, the British government, that took that initiative.
sentences.zh: 是他们，英国政府，采取了这一主动行动。

sentences.en: So everything thereafter, from John Adams' point of view, was merely reactive on the part of the rebels.
sentences.zh: 所以从约翰·亚当斯的角度来看，此后的一切对于叛乱者来说仅仅是反应性的。

sentences.en: Because he's conservative and he doesn't want to do anything so subversive as to declare independence himself.
sentences.zh: 因为他很保守，不想做任何像自己宣布独立那样颠覆性的事情。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, by this stage, he thinks a formal declaration of independence is certainly going to happen eventually, and he's keen to think of what a constitution will look like
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这个阶段，他认为正式宣布独立最终肯定会发生，他很热衷于思考宪法会是什么样子

sentences.en: in that new state.
sentences.zh: 在那个新国家里。

sentences.en: But he is pleased that, as it were, not just the first shot, but the declaration of war has come, as he understands it, from London and not from the colonies.
sentences.zh: 但他很高兴，正如他所理解的那样，不仅是第一枪，连宣战都是来自伦敦，而不是来自殖民地。

sentences.en: And he's not wrong to think that.
sentences.zh: 他这样想并没有错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because declaring a blockade is an act of war.
sentences.zh: 因为宣布封锁就是一种战争行为。

sentences.en: And that is what the British government does at the end of 1775.
sentences.zh: 这就是英国政府在1775年底所做的事情。

sentences.en: But there are more radical figures, I mean, we've talked about pain, but there are more radical figures who are actually American.
sentences.zh: 但还有一些更激进的人物，我的意思是，我们之前谈到了潘恩，但还有一些实际上是美国人的更激进的人物。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I guess the most celebrated of these is Thomas Jefferson, who is the man who will write the first draft of the Declaration of Independence.
sentences.zh: 我想其中最著名的是托马斯·杰斐逊，他就是起草《独立宣言》初稿的人。

sentences.en: So what has he been up to in the build-up to the war?
sentences.zh: 那么他在战争爆发前都在忙些什么呢？

sentences.en: And then what is he doing in the summer of 1776?
sentences.zh: 他在1776年夏天又在做什么？

sentences.en: Jefferson is a very interesting figure.
sentences.zh: 杰斐逊是一个非常有趣的人物。

sentences.en: The closest the American Revolution comes to kind of
sentences.zh: 他是美国革命中最接近那种

sentences.en: Robespierrean figure, although in a way that's rather flattering to Jefferson, makes him more of a man of action than he probably was.
sentences.zh: 罗伯斯庇尔式的人物，尽管从某种程度上说，这对杰斐逊来说是一种恭维，让他看起来比实际更像一个行动派。

sentences.en: I mean, he was a very privileged Virginia planter, slaveholder, who thought of himself as an intellectual, a man of the Enlightenment, a cosmopolitan figure,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是一位享有特权的弗吉尼亚种植园主和奴隶主，他自认为是知识分子、启蒙运动的拥护者、世界主义者，

sentences.en: steeped in the new ideas, and convinced that he and his generation, and he certainly felt himself to be the head of his generation,
sentences.zh: 沉浸在新思想中，并坚信他和他的那一代人——他当然认为自己是那一代人的领袖——

sentences.en: had an opportunity which had rarely, if ever, in human history come before, an opportunity to, in a painite way, begin the world anew, to start a new page,
sentences.zh: 拥有一个人类历史上罕见、甚至从未有过的机会，一个以潘恩的方式，让世界重新开始，翻开新的一页的机会，

sentences.en: and reinvent what it meant to be human.
sentences.zh: 并重塑人类的意义。

sentences.en: And he loved talking in these kinds of ways, and many people found that very inspiring.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢用这种方式交谈，许多人觉得这非常鼓舞人心。

sentences.en: And he was a great wordsmith.
sentences.zh: 他是一位伟大的文字大师。

sentences.en: And we see that in the preamble to the Declaration of Independence, which is obviously a beautifully written, sublime document, rightly famous and revered over the last 250 years.
sentences.zh: 我们在《独立宣言》的序言中看到了这一点，这显然是一份文笔优美、崇高的文件，在过去250年里一直享有盛誉并受到尊崇。

sentences.en: The quality of his prose was exceptional.
sentences.zh: 他的文笔质量非常出色。

sentences.en: And why is it Jefferson?
sentences.zh: 为什么偏偏是杰斐逊呢？

sentences.en: And so, first of all, well, why did Congress decide they need a Declaration of Independence?
sentences.zh: 首先，国会为什么要决定他们需要一份《独立宣言》？

sentences.en: I mean, because there are some people, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，因为有些人并不赞同，不是吗？

sentences.en: I think New York, maybe Delaware.
sentences.zh: 我想纽约可能就是，也许还有特拉华州。

sentences.en: Some of the colonies are a little bit more dragging their heels about it, don't think it's the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 有些殖民地在这一点上有些拖后腿，认为这不是正确的做法。

sentences.en: Well, because I was amazed that by the 1st of July, only nine of the 13 states have basically signed up to the separation from Britain.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为我很惊讶，到7月1日，13个州中只有9个基本签署了脱离英国的协议。

sentences.en: I think it was the 2nd of July that the motion was passed to formally constitute these new...
sentences.zh: 我想是在7月2日，动议通过了正式成立这些新的……

sentences.en: Well, because there's a brilliant comment in Holton's book where he describes how John Adams, again, writes about this decision on the 2nd of July
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为霍尔顿的书里有一段精彩的评论，他描述了约翰·亚当斯是如何再次写到7月2日的这个决定，

sentences.en: to declare independence and how it will be celebrated with shows, games, sports, guns, bells, bonfires, and illuminations from one end of this continent to the other.
sentences.zh: 即宣布独立，以及它将如何在这个大陆的每一个角落通过表演、游戏、体育、枪炮、钟声、篝火和灯火来庆祝。

sentences.en: Whereas, in fact, it's the Declaration of Independence, of course, on the 4th of July that is celebrated.
sentences.zh: 而事实上，当然是7月4日的《独立宣言》才被庆祝。

sentences.en: He says Americans celebrate the press release rather than the act itself.
sentences.zh: 他说美国人庆祝的是新闻稿，而不是行动本身。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: Why do they need a Declaration of Independence?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么需要《独立宣言》？

sentences.en: You know, a declaration de facto already existed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，事实上已经存在一种事实上的独立了。

sentences.en: In Thomas Jefferson's minds, that had been the status quo anti-anyway, as we've talked about in previous episodes.
sentences.zh: 在托马斯·杰斐逊看来，正如我们之前几集所谈到的，那已经是战前的现状了。

sentences.en: Well, you need all the states together, though, don't you?
sentences.zh: 嗯，但你需要所有州团结一致，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you need all the states to agree because otherwise they can be picked off much more readily if they haven't signed up to a kind of central declaration.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你需要所有州达成一致，否则如果他们没有签署某种中央宣言，就更容易被各个击破。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the press release, as you call it, or as Woody Halton calls it, is important because it's a manifesto.
sentences.zh: 而你所说的新闻稿，或者伍迪·霍尔顿所称的那样，之所以重要，是因为它是一份宣言。

sentences.en: It's a statement of principle, and it's a justification for what they're doing, aimed in no small part at Paris.
sentences.zh: 它是一份原则声明，是对他们所作所为的辩护，很大程度上是针对巴黎的。

sentences.en: At this point, the Americans knew that if they were going to engage in what they imagined would be a difficult and potentially long military engagement with the British,
sentences.zh: 在这一点上，美国人知道，如果他们要进行一场他们预想中与英国人之间艰难且可能旷日持久的军事对抗，

sentences.en: they were going to need support from France.
sentences.zh: 他们将需要法国的支持。

sentences.en: So it was a kind of justification, which was necessary for diplomatic purposes, but internally within the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种辩护，出于外交目的是必要的，但在美国内部也是如此。

sentences.en: And the key thing about the Declaration of Independence and what makes it new is that it is the king that's the target of the grievances.
sentences.zh: 关于《独立宣言》的关键点以及使其具有创新意义的地方在于，国王是他们不满的目标。

sentences.en: It's not parliament.
sentences.zh: 而不是议会。

sentences.en: And it had to be the king.
sentences.zh: 而且必须是国王。

sentences.en: It had to be the king because by this point, they were attempting to secede from the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 必须是国王，因为到这个时候，他们正试图脱离大英帝国。

sentences.en: Up until this point, they had been saying, we can be effectively a self-governing dominion within the British Empire, and therefore, we will still owe loyalty to the king.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，他们一直说，我们可以成为大英帝国境内有效的自治领，因此，我们仍然效忠于国王。

sentences.en: In July 1776, they were saying, no, no, no, we are going to create our own empire.
sentences.zh: 而在1776年7月，他们说，不，不，不，我们要建立我们自己的帝国。

sentences.en: And that was often the word that was used, and that was always the word that was used in London, creating their own empire, American empire.
sentences.zh: 这通常是当时使用的词，也是伦敦一直使用的词，建立他们自己的帝国，美利坚帝国。

sentences.en: So therefore, they had to throw off allegiance to the king, and therefore, it was necessary for them to turn King George III into this tyrannical figure,
sentences.zh: 因此，他们必须抛弃对国王的效忠，因此，他们有必要将乔治三世国王塑造成一个暴君形象，

sentences.en: necessary in order to justify to the world as well as to themselves what they were doing, just as in the same way it had been necessary in the 1640s
sentences.zh: 这对于向世界以及他们自己证明他们的行为是必要的，就像17世纪40年代对于议会派来说，

sentences.en: for the parliamentary side to focus on the king in the end and why it was necessary for the king to die in the 1640s in order to justify what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 最终必须聚焦于国王，以及为什么17世纪40年代国王必须死，以证明他们行为的正当性一样。

sentences.en: And in propagandistic terms, isn't the effect of that of proclaiming itself a republic as opposed to a monarchy?
sentences.zh: 从宣传的角度来看，宣布自己是一个共和国而不是君主国，难道没有这种效果吗？

sentences.en: It's backward-looking, because they can then invoke the Roman example, the Roman republic that expelled its king, and it can draw on all that kind of classical language,
sentences.zh: 这是向后看的，因为他们可以援引罗马的例子，那个驱逐了国王的罗马共和国，并可以利用所有那种古典语言，

sentences.en: elevating freedom and liberty and virtue.
sentences.zh: 提升自由、解放和美德。

sentences.en: But it's also, I think you could use the word progressive without too much risk of anachronism, that it's signing itself up to the more progressive element,
sentences.zh: 但我认为你也可以使用“进步”这个词，而不会有太大的时代错误风险，因为它是在签署加入更进步的元素，

sentences.en: the more radical element of the Enlightenment, and identifying America, the new world, as a kind of, you know, the best hope for humanity, that it has cast off the chains,
sentences.zh: 启蒙运动中更激进的元素，并将美国——这个新世界——定义为一种，你知道，人类最好的希望，它已经挣脱了枷锁，

sentences.en: that once again it's a city on a hill, offer an example to the old world.
sentences.zh: 它再次成为山巅之城，为旧世界提供了一个榜样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And that liberty has fled from its...
sentences.zh: 而自由已经从它的……

sentences.en: Yeah, so back to the pain comments.
sentences.zh: 是的，回到潘恩的评论上。

sentences.en: ...has fled from England and has taken up refuge in the new world, exactly.
sentences.zh: ……已经从英国逃离，并在新世界找到了避难所，没错。

sentences.en: So Adam, I mean, different historians have different takes on this.
sentences.zh: 所以亚当，我的意思是，不同的历史学家对此有不同的看法。

sentences.en: So for example, Gordon Wood, he's written lots about how the language of the Declaration, the language of the Revolution, in fact, is rooted in what he sees as the...
sentences.zh: 例如，戈登·伍德，他写了很多关于《独立宣言》的语言、革命的语言，事实上，是如何植根于他所认为的……

sentences.en: what lots of historians see as the kind of country, oppositional tradition, which is a kind of, itself, an attempt to preserve what people see
sentences.zh: 许多历史学家所认为的那种乡村、反对派传统，这本身就是一种试图保护人们所认为的

sentences.en: as the good old cause of 17th century England.
sentences.zh: 17世纪英国“美好的旧事业”的尝试。

sentences.en: So there's that, but there's also the Enlightenment, and let's say the French Enlightenment,
sentences.zh: 所以有这一点，但也有启蒙运动，比如法国启蒙运动，

sentences.en: Voltaire, Montesquieu, these characters, and there's John Locke and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 伏尔泰、孟德斯鸠这些人物，还有约翰·洛克等等。

sentences.en: So which of these traditions do you think is...
sentences.zh: 那么你认为这些传统中哪一个是……

sentences.en: can we say which is the more important?
sentences.zh: 我们能说哪一个更重要吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, there's also absolutely the biblical traditions that are deriving from the Puritan and the Quaker inheritance as well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，绝对还有源自清教徒和贵格会遗产的圣经传统。

sentences.en: Tom, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, but the rights of man, the fact that the creator endows
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，但是人权，造物主赋予

sentences.en: human beings with rights...
sentences.zh: 人类权利的事实……

sentences.en: Even though a lot of them are deists, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 尽管他们中很多人是自然神论者，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, but it's still...
sentences.zh: 是的，但它仍然……

sentences.en: that that idea is being framed in a way that can appeal to both Quakers in Philadelphia and Puritans in New England, but it's clearly very biblical.
sentences.zh: 那个想法被以一种既能吸引费城的贵格会教徒，又能吸引新英格兰的清教徒的方式构建出来，但它显然是非常符合圣经的。

sentences.en: So, Adam, untangle some of those strands for us.
sentences.zh: 所以，亚当，为我们理清其中一些脉络吧。

sentences.en: I mean, the Declaration of Independence itself is clearly Lockean.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，《独立宣言》本身显然是洛克式的。

sentences.en: It's making a Lockean argument about the social contract, that it has been broken, and that's the core justification for setting up a new government.
sentences.zh: 它提出了一个关于社会契约的洛克式论点，即契约已经被打破，这是建立新政府的核心理由。

sentences.en: And this is not accidental.
sentences.zh: 这并非偶然。

sentences.en: I mean, not just Jefferson, but these other elite figures gathered together in Philadelphia had read these tracts or at least knew enough about them
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，不仅是杰斐逊，聚集在费城的其他精英人物也读过这些小册子，或者至少对它们有足够的了解，

sentences.en: to be able to speak competently about them.
sentences.zh: 能够胜任地谈论它们。

sentences.en: They could do a podcast about them, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们可以做一个关于这些内容的播客。

sentences.en: They could definitely do a podcast about them.
sentences.zh: 他们绝对可以做一个关于这些内容的播客。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They knew how to fake it.
sentences.zh: 他们知道如何装模作样。

sentences.en: And so, I mean, yeah, I don't know how far...
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，是的，我不知道在多大程度上……

sentences.en: I mean, if you're just asking about that document itself, it's easy to root it in those Enlightenment thinkers, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你只是问那份文件本身，多米尼克，很容易将其归根于那些启蒙思想家。

sentences.en: And the broader pamphlet literature, and this is where Gordon Wood and his mentor, Bernard Balin, is making this argument about the Whig country tradition and the good old cause
sentences.zh: 还有更广泛的小册子文献，这就是戈登·伍德和他的导师伯纳德·贝林提出关于辉格党乡村传统和“美好的旧事业”论点的地方，

sentences.en: of the 17th century.
sentences.zh: 即17世纪的传统。

sentences.en: They're looking at the, not just at the Declaration of Independence, but all of the pamphlets published in the preceding 15 years.
sentences.zh: 他们看的不仅仅是《独立宣言》，还有过去15年里出版的所有小册子。

sentences.en: And they're looking at all, and they're seeing, what they're seeing in that language is the 17th century and early 18th century English language of liberty,
sentences.zh: 他们审视了一切，他们所看到的，在那语言中看到的是17世纪和18世纪初的英国自由语言，

sentences.en: Whiggish language of liberty.
sentences.zh: 辉格党的自由语言。

sentences.en: And so what that does is to give to the revolution a functioning state, I mean, even if very still inchoate, but also a kind of ideology that people can now increasingly sign up to
sentences.zh: 所以这样做的好处是为革命提供了一个运作中的国家，我的意思是，即使仍然非常不成熟，但也提供了一种人们现在可以越来越多地认同的意识形态，

sentences.en: and which gives a kind of motivational justification for what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 并为他们的所作所为提供了一种激励性的辩护。

sentences.en: Yes, and we hold these truths to be self-evident that all men are created equal.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们认为这些真理是不言而喻的，人人生而平等。

sentences.en: That lying from the preamble to the Declaration of Independence has, of course, frequently been cited as effectively the ideological underpinning of the United States.
sentences.zh: 那句出自《独立宣言》序言的话，当然经常被引用为美国实际上在意识形态上的基石。

sentences.en: And that is what makes it possible, among other things, but that's the core of it, to think of the American project as an ideological project, a project that is dedicated,
sentences.zh: 而这正是使人们能够将美国项目视为一个意识形态项目的原因，除其他因素外，这是核心，一个致力于……的项目，

sentences.en: and this is actually an Abraham Lincoln usage, right, at Lincoln and Gettysburg in 1863, turned the Declaration of Independence.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是亚伯拉罕·林肯的用法，对吧，林肯在1863年的葛底斯堡演说中，转向了《独立宣言》。

sentences.en: He wasn't the only person to do it, but he turned the Declaration of Independence into this baptismal document for the nation, not the Articles of Confederation or the Constitution
sentences.zh: 他不是唯一这样做的人，但他将《独立宣言》变成了这个国家的洗礼文件，而不是《邦联条例》或《宪法》

sentences.en: or the Treaty of Paris or any of these other things in international law, but the Declaration of Independence because of that rousing preamble.
sentences.zh: 或《巴黎条约》或国际法中的任何其他东西，而是《独立宣言》，因为那段激动人心的序言。

sentences.en: And, of course, Martin Luther King in 1963 will also invoke it to talk about equality for black people.
sentences.zh: 当然，马丁·路德·金在1963年也会援引它来谈论黑人的平等。

sentences.en: A promissory note, as King calls it.
sentences.zh: 正如金所称的，一张期票。

sentences.en: We've come to cash the check, as he says in the March of Washington in 1963.
sentences.zh: 正如他在1963年华盛顿大游行中所说，我们来兑现这张支票。

sentences.en: But, Adam, I mean, that goes to the point, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 但是，亚当，我的意思是，这触及了重点，不是吗？

sentences.en: That that claim we hold that, you know, all men are created equal.
sentences.zh: 那个主张，我们认为，你知道，人人生而平等。

sentences.en: Some of them don't mean it.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人并不是真心的。

sentences.en: I mean, Jefferson himself has 600 slaves in his lifetime, and during his lifetime, I think he freed two.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，杰斐逊本人一生拥有600名奴隶，而在他的一生中，我想他只释放了两个。

sentences.en: So, Washington has a mouthful of other people's teeth.
sentences.zh: 所以，华盛顿满嘴都是别人的牙齿。

sentences.en: I mean, these are, I mean, this is the criticism that is made of them in the 21st century by, you know, we talked last time about the 1619 projects and so on,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些是……我的意思是，这是21世纪人们对他们的批评，你知道，我们上次谈到了1619项目等等，

sentences.en: that the Declaration of Independence is a conservative document, some people would say.
sentences.zh: 有些人会说《独立宣言》是一份保守的文件。

sentences.en: But, Dominic, it's also a criticism being made at the time.
sentences.zh: 但是，多米尼克，这也是当时人们提出的批评。

sentences.en: I mean, we talked about Dr. Johnson in the previous episode.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在上一集谈到了约翰逊博士。

sentences.en: So, Adam, they had a section on slavery which they cut out.
sentences.zh: 所以，亚当，他们有一段关于奴隶制的章节被删掉了。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 那是真的吗？

sentences.en: That Jefferson himself wrote and then cut out?
sentences.zh: 是杰斐逊本人写的然后又删掉的吗？

sentences.en: And I think it was by far, in Jefferson's original draft, it was by far the longest of the list of grievances, some of which are slightly tendentious
sentences.zh: 我想在杰斐逊的初稿中，这绝对是所有不满清单中最长的一项，其中一些略带偏见，

sentences.en: and all of which are slightly hyperbolic.
sentences.zh: 而且所有这些都略显夸张。

sentences.en: That was the longest one, the one condemning the king for imposing slavery on the colonies.
sentences.zh: 那是其中最长的一项，谴责国王将奴隶制强加给殖民地。

sentences.en: That was cut out by the convention.
sentences.zh: 那一段被大会删掉了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, this is, I mean, the Declaration of Independence is really, in a way, I mean, it's the most significant, single most significant text, parche, Woody Holton,
sentences.zh: 所以，这是……我的意思是，《独立宣言》在某种程度上确实是，我的意思是，它是美国历史上最重要的、单一最重要的文本，伍迪·霍尔顿，

sentences.en: you know, in the history of America.
sentences.zh: 你知道。

sentences.en: So, I think it's worth looking at in the detail that we have done.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为值得我们像这样详细地研究它。

sentences.en: But we must remember that there is simultaneously a war going on which we've barely touched on.
sentences.zh: 但我们必须记住，同时还有一场战争正在进行，我们几乎没有触及到这一点。

sentences.en: So, why don't we take a break now and when we come back, let's look at the course of the war and what is going on.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们现在休息一下，回来后，让我们看看战争的进程以及正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Welcome back to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的其余部分》。

sentences.en: So, we've been talking about the Declaration of Independence which Congress votes in favour of independence on the 2nd of July.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们一直在谈论《独立宣言》，国会在7月2日投票赞成独立。

sentences.en: Two days later, it's the press release,
sentences.zh: 两天后，就是新闻稿，

sentences.en: as we were saying.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说的那样。

sentences.en: And there are bells ringing in cannon going off in Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 费城钟声齐鸣，大炮轰鸣。

sentences.en: A few days later,
sentences.zh: 几天后，

sentences.en: George Washington reads the declaration to his troops in New York and they pull down the statue of George III.
sentences.zh: 乔治·华盛顿在纽约向他的部队宣读了宣言，他们推倒了乔治三世的雕像。

sentences.en: But of course, I mean, that's a reminder that there is, as Tom said just before the break, a war going on.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我的意思是，这提醒我们，正如汤姆在休息前所说，战争正在进行。

sentences.en: Because they melt it down, don't they, and turn the statue into bullets.
sentences.zh: 因为他们把它熔化了，不是吗，把雕像变成了子弹。

sentences.en: They do indeed.
sentences.zh: 他们确实这样做了。

sentences.en: Exactly, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，是的。

sentences.en: And even as they do that, the 30,000 British troops, which is, I believe, the largest European force ever sent overseas, which gives you a scale, I suppose, of the challenge
sentences.zh: 即使在他们这样做的时候，3万名英国军队——我相信这是有史以来派往海外的最大规模的欧洲军队，这让你了解了挑战的规模，我想，

sentences.en: that is facing Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 大不列颠所面临的挑战。

sentences.en: 30,000 British troops are coming ashore on Staten Island.
sentences.zh: 3万名英国军队正在斯塔滕岛登陆。

sentences.en: And the British, so they've said, sod Boston,
sentences.zh: 英国人说，去他的波士顿，

sentences.en: Boston is gone.
sentences.zh: 波士顿已经丢了。

sentences.en: The priority now is New York.
sentences.zh: 现在的重点是纽约。

sentences.en: That's right, isn't it, Adam?
sentences.zh: 那是对的，不是吗，亚当？

sentences.en: Yes, they've given up on Boston.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们已经放弃了波士顿。

sentences.en: And the question now is, can they isolate New England?
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是，他们能孤立新英格兰吗？

sentences.en: Can they use New York as a base from which they can take Philadelphia, which was functionally the capital of this newly declared independent country or nation or whatever it was
sentences.zh: 他们能利用纽约作为基地来夺取费城吗？费城在功能上是这个新宣布独立的国家或民族，或者无论它是什么，

sentences.en: or empire?
sentences.zh: 或者帝国，的首都。

sentences.en: And they knew they had a formal opponent in the Continental Army under the command of George Washington.
sentences.zh: 他们知道他们在乔治·华盛顿指挥下的大陆军中有一个正式的对手。

sentences.en: They had reason to believe, not least because of the Battle of Bunker Hill, that they shouldn't underestimate this enemy.
sentences.zh: 他们有理由相信，不仅仅是因为邦克山战役，他们不应该低估这个敌人。

sentences.en: But everything else was really still in flux at this point.
sentences.zh: 但当时其他一切都还处于变动之中。

sentences.en: What kind of a war this was going to be?
sentences.zh: 这将会是一场什么样的战争？

sentences.en: What role, if any, the Navy was going to be able to play?
sentences.zh: 海军如果能发挥作用，会是什么角色？

sentences.en: How much resource could be diverted from the protection of British colonial interests elsewhere in the world?
sentences.zh: 能从世界其他地方保护英国殖民利益的资源中，挪出多少资源来？

sentences.en: You know, how important in the end was this going to be?
sentences.zh: 你知道，最终这到底有多重要？

sentences.en: How many, how high were taxes going to go in Britain yet again in order to pay for another war in North America?
sentences.zh: 为了支付在北美发动的另一场战争，英国的税收还要涨多少、涨多高？

sentences.en: All of these things were still to be determined in 1776.
sentences.zh: 所有这些在1776年时都尚未确定。

sentences.en: And so two questions
sentences.zh: 所以有两个问题

sentences.en: one is, are they conscious even at this stage about that the French and the Spanish might pile in?
sentences.zh: 一个是，他们在这个阶段是否已经意识到法国和西班牙可能会插手？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That is their big fear.
sentences.zh: 那是他们最大的恐惧。

sentences.en: Of course, the King and Lord North, they don't want to lose the 13 colonies anyway.
sentences.zh: 当然，国王和诺斯勋爵无论如何都不想失去这13个殖民地。

sentences.en: There's a huge issue of pride and ego and patriotism and all these kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 这涉及巨大的自尊、虚荣、爱国主义以及所有这类问题。

sentences.en: But there is a basic geopolitical anxiety.
sentences.zh: 但存在一种基本的地缘政治焦虑。

sentences.en: They previously fought this highly successful war, the Seven Years' War, expelled the French from North America.
sentences.zh: 他们之前打赢了那场非常成功的七年战争，将法国人赶出了北美。

sentences.en: The obvious danger here is that this is going to provide an opening for the French to repossess part of their or all of their former colonial possessions in North America.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的危险在于，这会给法国人提供一个机会，让他们夺回在北美部分或全部的前殖民地。

sentences.en: So they have to keep some troops back.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须留下一部分军队。

sentences.en: They have to defend Britain from French invasion, conceivably, and they have to defend the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 他们必须防范法国可能发动的入侵，还要保卫加勒比地区。

sentences.en: They need to in both instances because there is, I mean, that's the real, that's the real worry is the loss of the Caribbean islands.
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下他们都需要（军队），因为真正的担忧是失去加勒比群岛。

sentences.en: And of course, there is a genuine threat of invasion after the French enter the war in the late 1770s.
sentences.zh: 当然，在18世纪70年代末法国参战后，确实存在真正的入侵威胁。

sentences.en: So they're not wrong to think that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们这样想并没有错。

sentences.en: So my second question very quickly is, are there some people in Britain who think, okay, cut our losses now, the thing is gone, this has not worked out,
sentences.zh: 那么我的第二个问题很快就来了，英国是否有人认为，好吧，现在止损吧，事情已经过去了，这行不通了，

sentences.en: let's call the whole thing off?
sentences.zh: 我们干脆放弃吧？

sentences.en: I mean, the impression I get is that actually quite a number of the high command think that.
sentences.zh: 我的印象是，实际上相当多的高级指挥官是这样想的。

sentences.en: A lot of people think that and Lord Chatham, former William Pitt basically thinks that.
sentences.zh: 很多人都这么想，前首相威廉·皮特（查塔姆伯爵）基本上也是这么认为的。

sentences.en: And this is one of the problems that the king now has is that the king is really committed to suppressing this rebellion.
sentences.zh: 而国王现在面临的问题之一是，他真的致力于镇压这场叛乱。

sentences.en: And the only prime minister he can work with to achieve that goal is Lord North.
sentences.zh: 为了实现这一目标，他唯一能合作的首相就是诺斯勋爵。

sentences.en: So when Lord North keeps on saying, I just can't cope with this anymore, please, please, please let me resign at the end of the next parliamentary session.
sentences.zh: 所以当诺斯勋爵一直说，我实在应付不了这个了，请务必、务必、务必让我下届议会会议结束时辞职。

sentences.en: And the king keeps on saying no because he knows that the only alternative is to invite one of the opposition factional leaders whose policy will be a peace policy.
sentences.zh: 而国王一直说不，因为他知道唯一的选择就是邀请反对派领袖之一，而他们的政策将是和平政策。

sentences.en: So just on George III who's oddly being absent from almost all the story, at this point is George III genuinely a factor in that he is his stubbornness,
sentences.zh: 那么，关于乔治三世，他在整个故事中奇怪地缺席了，此时乔治三世是否真的是一个因素，因为他的固执，

sentences.en: his, you know, you can call it his patriotism if you like, or his small c conservatism or his sense of pride.
sentences.zh: 他的，你知道，你可以称之为爱国主义，或者他的小c保守主义，或者他的自尊心。

sentences.en: Is that really a factor in keeping the British fighting?
sentences.zh: 这真的是让英国继续战斗的一个因素吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I think it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为是。

sentences.en: I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我认为是。

sentences.en: And I think actually that's the right way of putting it, Dominic, in that really up until now the irony is that the king hasn't been a major player.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为多米尼克，这样说很准确，讽刺的是，直到现在国王都不是主要参与者。

sentences.en: And obviously he's not really in control of government policy.
sentences.zh: 显然他并没有真正控制政府政策。

sentences.en: He can only implement things through the cabinet.
sentences.zh: 他只能通过内阁来实施事务。

sentences.en: And he's extremely conscious of constitutional prerogatives and precedents.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常在意宪法特权和先例。

sentences.en: But he really does very, very, very strongly believe that the Americans should not be allowed to become independent.
sentences.zh: 但他确实非常、非常、非常强烈地认为不应该允许美国人独立。

sentences.en: And so he works very, very hard to, you know, basically keep, put some backbone into his cabinet ministers.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常、非常努力地，你知道，基本上保持，给他的内阁大臣们注入一些骨气。

sentences.en: So he is a factor there.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实是一个因素。

sentences.en: So the issue for the British, how on earth are they going to get America back?
sentences.zh: 那么对英国人来说，问题是，他们到底要怎样才能夺回美国？

sentences.en: Because they won the Battle of Bunker Hill, but then they had to evacuate Boston.
sentences.zh: 因为他们赢得了邦克山战役，但随后不得不撤离波士顿。

sentences.en: So in a sense, winning a battle isn't enough.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，赢得一场战斗是不够的。

sentences.en: You are only as good as the territory you're holding.
sentences.zh: 你拥有的领土决定了你的实力。

sentences.en: And therefore, the question is, what strategy can they put in that would enable them to expand beyond the few kind of toeholds that they have along the coast?
sentences.zh: 因此，问题在于，他们能制定什么战略，使他们能够扩展到海岸边那几个立足点之外？

sentences.en: And so New York becomes basically the kind of the focus for their hopes.
sentences.zh: 所以纽约基本上成了他们希望的焦点。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: One answer to the question of what strategy they can do is that they could destroy Washington's army, the Continental Army.
sentences.zh: 关于他们能采取什么战略的问题，一个答案是他们可以摧毁华盛顿的军队，即大陆军。

sentences.en: And they could have, and they actually could have done so.
sentences.zh: 他们本可以，而且实际上本可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, one of the what-ifs in this story is that there were moments early in the war, in 1776 and 1777 anyway, when General Howe and General Clinton,
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，这个故事中的假设之一是，在战争初期，无论如何是在1776年和1777年，豪将军和克林顿将军，

sentences.en: who were the two key military commanders in that region could potentially have cut off the Continental Army and destroyed it, potentially even captured
sentences.zh: 作为该地区两名关键的军事指挥官，本可以切断大陆军并摧毁它，甚至可能俘虏

sentences.en: George Washington.
sentences.zh: 乔治·华盛顿。

sentences.en: And the whole course of the war could have looked extreme, could have looked very different if that had happened.
sentences.zh: 如果发生了这种情况，整个战争的进程看起来可能会非常、非常不同。

sentences.en: I mean, famously, they could perhaps have prevented the Continental Army from evacuating from Manhattan and they didn't do so.
sentences.zh: 我是说，众所周知，他们本可以阻止大陆军从曼哈顿撤离，但他们没有这样做。

sentences.en: And there are very good reasons why they didn't do so based on logistics and supply and so on.
sentences.zh: 而且他们没有这样做的原因非常充分，基于后勤和补给等等。

sentences.en: But nevertheless,
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，

sentences.en: Washington was able to escape.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿还是得以逃脱。

sentences.en: But that's a key moment, isn't it, Adam?
sentences.zh: 但那是一个关键时刻，不是吗，亚当？

sentences.en: Because they had landed at Staten Island.
sentences.zh: 因为他们已经在斯塔滕岛登陆了。

sentences.en: They have this huge battle on Long Island, which I think is the biggest single battle of the war, which puts the British win.
sentences.zh: 他们在长岛进行了一场巨大的战役，我认为这是战争中规模最大的一场战役，英国人赢了。

sentences.en: Half of Washington's army is left trapped in Brooklyn.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿的一半军队被困在布鲁克林。

sentences.en: And then the British hesitate.
sentences.zh: 然后英国人犹豫了。

sentences.en: And one reason they hesitate is actually going back to something that Tom, I think, said earlier on, which is that a lot of the British commanders are actually quite ambivalent
sentences.zh: 他们犹豫的一个原因实际上回到了汤姆早些时候说的话，那就是许多英国指挥官实际上对

sentences.en: about the whole business.
sentences.zh: 整个事情相当矛盾。

sentences.en: So General Howe, his brother is Admiral Howe, who's in charge of the Navy, and he used to play chess with Benjamin Franklin when they were in London.
sentences.zh: 所以豪将军，他的兄弟是负责海军的豪海军上将，他们以前在伦敦时常和本杰明·富兰克林下棋。

sentences.en: So they're all quite sort of sympathetic to the Americans.
sentences.zh: 所以他们都对美国人相当同情。

sentences.en: Yes, they'd all opposed most of this legislation we've been talking about in previous episodes.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们都反对我们在前几集里讨论过的大部分立法。

sentences.en: All of these people.
sentences.zh: 所有这些人。

sentences.en: I mean, it is amazing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太令人惊讶了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah, they didn't really want the British to be in this situation.
sentences.zh: 是啊，他们并不真的希望英国陷入这种境地。

sentences.en: Even General Cornwallis, who's famous later on, he had opposed, he'd voted against the Stamp Act.
sentences.zh: 即使是后来出名的康沃利斯将军，他也曾反对过，他曾投票反对《印花税法案》。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Incredibly.
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信。

sentences.en: But anyway, they have a peace conference on Staten Island, don't they?
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，他们在斯塔滕岛举行了和平会议，不是吗？

sentences.en: They meet John Adams and Benjamin Franklin, who meets his old chess sparring partner on Staten Island.
sentences.zh: 他们见到了约翰·亚当斯和本杰明·富兰克林，后者在斯塔滕岛见到了他以前的棋友。

sentences.en: And the British say to them, listen, let's just shake hands and pretend this was all a bad dream.
sentences.zh: 英国人对他们说，听着，让我们握手言和，假装这一切只是一场噩梦。

sentences.en: And they basically say the king will pardon you.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上说国王会赦免你们。

sentences.en: But the Americans, is it just that they're too far gone now?
sentences.zh: 但美国人，是因为他们现在已经走得太远了吗？

sentences.en: Well, the Americans have already declared independence.
sentences.zh: 嗯，美国人已经宣布独立了。

sentences.en: From their point of view now, the only terms for peace will be recognition of American independence.
sentences.zh: 从他们的角度来看，现在唯一的和平条件就是承认美国独立。

sentences.en: And that, of course, is not something that the British military commanders are authorised or would have wanted to concede even if they had been authorised to do so.
sentences.zh: 而这当然不是英国军事指挥官被授权或愿意承认的事情，即使他们被授权这样做。

sentences.en: So it goes nowhere.
sentences.zh: 所以这毫无进展。

sentences.en: But could, I mean, if George III had been a tyrant and the British had been the monsters from a Mel Gibson film, presumably they would have just captured or killed
sentences.zh: 但如果，我是说，如果乔治三世是个暴君，而英国人是梅尔·吉布森电影里的怪物，想必他们当时就会直接俘虏或杀死

sentences.en: the American delegates then and there, destroyed Washington's army, captured or killed him.
sentences.zh: 美国代表，摧毁华盛顿的军队，俘虏或杀死他。

sentences.en: And we'd be talking about a very different scenario, would we?
